title_en: Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei — smuggling of giant panda skins

full_text_en:
Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei — Smuggling Giant Panda Skin Case

Defendant: Chen Yonglin, male, 24 years old, native of Bao'an County, Guangdong Province, arrested on September 7, 1987.

Defendant: Chen Zupei, male, 27 years old, native of Bao'an County, Guangdong Province, arrested on September 7, 1987.

In the case of defendants Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei for smuggling giant panda skin, the Guangzhou People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province instituted a public prosecution before the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court on November 3, 1987. On November 11 of the same year, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court legally formed a collegial panel and conducted a public trial. The facts found by the court are as follows:

In December 1986, defendants Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei jointly purchased a motor vessel, "Bao'an 54013." On January 12, 1987, Chen Yonglin went to Shenzhen as agreed to meet with Hong Kong smuggler Chen Yaofu (at large). Chen Yaofu entrusted Chen Yonglin with smuggling one piece of rare animal skin to Hong Kong. Chen Yonglin consented. On the same day, Chen Yonglin informed Chen Zupei of Chen Yaofu's commission, and Chen Zupei also consented. At approximately 9:00 p.m. that evening, Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei went to the Shenzhen Bay Hotel as agreed to meet Chen Yaofu. After collusion, both parties agreed on the time and place for handing over the smuggled goods. At noon on January 13, Chen Yaofu placed one giant panda skin in a nylon bag at Shekou, Shenzhen, and handed it to Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei. Chen Yonglin instructed Chen Zupei to conceal the nylon bag in the interlayer hidden compartment of the motor vessel. Thereafter, the two drove the vessel, evading customs supervision, and illegally smuggled it out of the country via the Pearl River estuary. When the vessel reached the sea area near Dachan Island, it was intercepted by Guangzhou Customs with both the contraband and the offenders.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, the seized contraband, and other evidence. The defendants Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei also confessed to the crimes, which are sufficient for determination.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court is of the following opinion:

Defendants Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei, disregarding national laws and violating customs regulations, smuggled the rare animal giant panda skin out of the country, which constitutes the crime of smuggling as provided in Article 118 of the Criminal Law of the PRC. The giant panda is an extremely precious and rare wild animal. The defendants, knowing that panda skin could not be exported, nevertheless smuggled it out of the country, and the circumstances are especially serious. According to Article 1, Item 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Undermine the Economy, the defendants should be severely punished. The acts of Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei seriously disrupted social order; therefore, in accordance with Article 52 of the Criminal Law, deprivation of political rights may be imposed as a supplementary punishment. In accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law, the seized giant panda skin and the property used by the defendants for the crime shall be confiscated.

On November 25, 1987, based on the facts of the defendants' crimes, the circumstances, and the degree of harm to society, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgments respectively: Defendant Chen Yonglin was found guilty of smuggling and sentenced to twelve years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for four years; Defendant Chen Zupei was found guilty of smuggling and sentenced to ten years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for three years. The seized one piece of giant panda skin smuggled by Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei and the smuggler's tool, the motor vessel "Bao'an 54013," were ordered to be confiscated.

After the judgment at first instance, defendants Chen Yonglin and Chen Zupei did not appeal.
